cells.tense: You are sitting where a feeling gets weighed, and your hand is steady on it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Pick one arrangement between you and someone else — even when you made it, lopsided now — and end it on your side, no speech attached.
cells.core:
Feelings land in you whole. Somebody's hurt, somebody's anger, your own — none of it gets skipped, and none of it gets to tip what you decide. A thing is allowed to finish happening before you say what it was. Whoever is sitting across from you can feel they'll get a straight measure.

What that leaves sitting are the arrangements you set back when they were right. A split, a rule, a way of doing things between you and one other — even then, lopsided now, and you keep honouring it because ending it looks like a loss. It isn't. The other person knows it's finished; letting it go just says that you know too, with nothing else needing explaining.
cells.sheetLine: You take the feeling whole and still call it even.
cells.verb: feeling it through and still calling it even
cells.place: where what couldn't hold has just come down, and the ground is clear

cells.tense: You will have it settled before the hurt has finished arriving in the room.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: When someone's hurt reaches you this week, keep it a full day without deciding whether it was fair — hold it as something carried, not something judged.
cells.core:
The weighing has got out ahead of the feeling. Something lands — someone's hurt, someone's anger — and before it has had its hour the answer has come, whole, with the proportionate call attached. You're usually right. Being right early is still early. The ruling comes down over them like a decision they didn't ask for, and they stop bringing you anything raw.

Hold instead. The next weight that comes to you, carry it the way a mason carries a stone up a stair — a load, no ruling attached, not yet a wall. Give the hurt the full day. Nothing about the call goes worse for waiting, and whoever it concerns can hear it better once you say it later.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling it fair before it's finished hurting.
cells.verb: feeling it through and still calling it even
cells.place: where what couldn't hold has just come down, and the ground is clear

cells.tense: You stood at a door that closed behind you and you have not turned round from it.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take one lopsided situation near you and put down what happened, each piece in order, feeling words left off the page — then look at what you wrote.
cells.core:
Something came down here, or came apart, and the fairness that used to move in you has gone quiet with it. The lopsidedness is still visible to you. You see it and let it keep standing, and the people inside that arrangement go on living in it while nobody will call it what it is. The judging part isn't gone. It's parked at a door that's already shut.

Nerve would fix this, but nerve isn't the thing you reach for. Paper is. Write out one unfair situation — each piece of what happened, in order, feeling words nowhere on the page. You don't have to feel steady to make a list. Half the call is made by then, in your own handwriting, and you can see whether it holds.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the lopsided thing. You've stopped saying so.

cells.tense: You are the one who keeps things level, and you would tell anyone you aren't in it.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Hear a quarrel among the people around you to its end, as someone new to it, before you make your usual move to even it up.
cells.core:
Things among the people near you stay roughly level, and that is your doing — a word shifted here, a weight taken off someone there. Ask you and you weren't involved. It has gone on so long it runs without you watching it. Those who get kept level have not bought the story that you stay out; they can see whose hand moved the scale.

Listen instead of working. The next argument near you, hear it to the end as if you were new to it — the version before you smooth anything over. You'll catch the part you usually reach past, and you'll see your own hand from inside the work. Nothing else has to change.
